headline: CEO bullish on Saint Nicholas polymetallic project in Bosnia, citing up to 15% nickel, 9% lead/zinc, 6g/t gold on surface, first drilling in 56 years imminent, and $5M cash with no debt to fund all three assets
reasoning: Petar Tomasevic describes the Saint Nicholas asset in Republic of Srpska as potentially one of the highest-grade polymetallic assets in Europe, with historical 1970s drill holes showing up to 15% nickel, 9% lead and zinc from surface to 50m, and recently discovered gold (6g/t) and silver (1,300g/t) mineralisation. The company has secured a six-year land access agreement with vendors accepting equity rather than cash, preserving the company's ~$5M cash position for drilling. With a $20M market cap and no debt, management believes they have sufficient funds to drill all three Balkan assets by end of 2026. He draws a direct comparable to Adriatic Metals, which listed on ASX in 2018 for ~$20M and was acquired by Dundee for $2B in 2024, operating in the same Tethyan metallogenic belt. First drilling at Saint Nicholas is expected within two weeks.
quote: first of all, the, the 20 historical drill holes that's been done in the in the 70s have some of the highest grade nickel and antimony that I've seen in my lifetime. So there is up to 15% of nickel. There is a layer of, of, of base metals from surface to 50 metres where nickel sulphide mineralisation starts. So up to 9% lead and zinc. And we recently also discovered the gold and silver mineralisation, 6 grammes per tonne gold and 1300 grammes silver on surface. So very peculiar for that type of mineralization and I just can't wait to drill it and find out what's really underneath.
episode_title: Yugo Metals digs deeper into historic site

headline: ~$5M cash, no debt, funded to drill all three assets through first half of next year; re-testing historic drill results with modern methods and holds option to acquire land for modest consideration
reasoning: Yugo Metals has approximately $5 million in cash against a $20 million market cap, carries no debt, and management believes the company is sufficiently funded to drill all three assets through the first half of the following year. The company is listed on both the ASX and Frankfurt Stock Exchange. Management is re-twinning historic drill holes to validate results using modern testing methods. The company also holds an option to acquire the land outright for a modest sum, providing flexibility if an economic deposit is defined. Contractors accepted equity as payment, preserving cash flexibility.
